name: PhD in Neuroscience
detailsNote: The program page gives December 1 for the fall term without a year, so it is shown as a published date and is not confirmed for Fall 2027. How students are admitted (program or lab), GRE, letters and funding are not stated for this program on the pages read.
summary: PhD in Neuroscience at Marquette University, a STEM-designated program. A recruitment committee reviews applications and selects applicants for phone and then on-campus interviews.

publishedDeadlines.label: Application deadline for the fall term (year not stated)
publishedDeadlines.note: Program page: "December 1: Application and application materials should be received to be considered for the fall term." Confirm Fall 2027.

timeline.interviews: The recruitment committee selects a sub-group for phone interviews, then applicants are selected for on-campus interviews.

english.toefl: 80 on the internet-based test, with at least 20 in each section (scale not stated on the page)
english.note: Required for international applicants whose language of instruction was not English. Scores may not be more than two years old. Some programs may require higher scores.

applicationFee.note: The FAQ says waivers are given only in a few circumstances: previous Marquette graduate students, current Marquette undergraduates or Marquette bachelor's graduates, McNair Scholars, and applicants who attended a Marquette campus visit event. International applicants should confirm eligibility.

documents: Transcripts from all previously attended institutions
Bachelor's degree in science, technology, engineering or mathematics from a regionally accredited institution (or an international equivalent)
requirements.note: The Graduate School FAQ says most programs require three letters of recommendation and that GRE requirements depend on the program; the neuroscience page does not say.

international.note: The program page says the program is STEM-designated and international students can apply for 36 months of Optional Practical Training.

sources.label: Graduate School FAQ: fee, waivers, English, letters
